status: Round 1 of 3: 4 of 8 runs scored (6:40 AM ET); the refiner, H3-decoder fine-tunes, text and DWD children are scored next
verdict: Not yet. On single-image latents a small new decoder beats H3's decoder on every metric, but by eye H3's decoder still looks better, and no sampling decoder has won by eye yet.
numbers: H3's decoder (single-image path, 7 repeated latent frames): PSNR 30.42 dB, DISTS 0.070, LPIPS-vgg 0.159, 714 ms per 512² image
pixreg, a 68 M regression decoder trained 70 min on 1 A100: PSNR 32.14 dB, DISTS 0.051, LPIPS-vgg 0.111, 51 ms; but blind judges preferred H3's decoder 28 to 4 (pixreg is blurrier)

pixflow, the same network as a flow sampler: one sample PSNR 30.49 dB (= H3), sharper (sharp_fft 0.92 vs 0.83); blind judges 11 vs 18 for H3 (not significant). The mean of 8 samples (32.18 dB) only restates the regression result
Caveat: H3's decoder in VIDEO mode (whole clip latent) gets 33.3 dB on the same frames, so its single-image path is handicapped; the video-latent comparison is round 2
§25 optimized latent through H3's decoder (12 images): 35.22 dB, DISTS 0.024: the regression upper bound
